items.title: 68190_Samuel
items.q: I started playing with Buster Smith at a place called Lucille's Paradise

ctx.x: None of the originals that were with him before. See, possibly getting a little ahead of my story, Harlan Leonard's band also -- the Kansas City Rockets also broke up in 1936, after our second unsuccessful trip to Chicago to try to make it big and I guess most of the guys figured, "Well, this is enough. We want to play music but we will also dedicate ourselves to making a living and getting the best out of it", and then we all branched off into smaller groups.

I started playing with Buster Smith at a place called Lucille's Paradise and Baby Lovett, Herman Walder, Jack Johnson, a little place there and Pete Johnson, the great Pete Walder Johnson, the boogie woogie piano player, and the brothers, Herman and Woodie, and I believe there were six members in that band, I think I named all six of them. Well they went to play at 12th and Truce at a place called the Spinning Wheel, and this was part of the band that was a part of Leonard's band; that is, the Kansas City…

Well, we'll come back to the Spinning Wheel when we get into the rooms that were in town that we're going to cover. That's very interesting, Crook's description of what happened to the Harlem Leonard great band. We'll be right back ladies and gentlemen.
